{
  "claims": [
    {
      "source_id": "fulltext:2603.03251",
      "quote": "While a verification is ongoing, the draft model predicts likely verification outcomes and prepares speculations pre-emptively for them.",
      "claim": "The SSD authors propose preparing draft continuations while target verification runs.",
      "relation": "supports",
      "conditions": "The actual verification outcome must be among the predicted outcomes for a prepared continuation to be usable immediately.",
      "reported_result": "The supplied excerpt describes the mechanism; this passage is not an implementation result.",
      "transfer_inference": "DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash could benefit if drafting waits on verification in its B200 deployment.",
      "limitations": "No such wait or measured vLLM bottleneck is supplied. The excerpt does not establish a B200 implementation or effect size."
    },
    {
      "source_id": "fulltext:2603.03251",
      "quote": "on average 30% faster than the strongest speculative decoding baselines and up to 5x faster than autoregressive generation",
      "claim": "The SSD authors report latency gains across datasets and model families.",
      "relation": "supports",
      "conditions": "Results are for the paper's evaluated setups.",
      "reported_result": "Author-reported average 30% gain over speculative decoding baselines and up to 5× over autoregressive generation.",
      "transfer_inference": "The result makes asynchronous speculation worth evaluating for latency.",
      "limitations": "The supplied excerpt does not identify DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, B200, the evaluated hardware, or the relevant workload and resource cost. Its speedups cannot be assigned to the target deployment."
    },
    {
      "source_id": "fulltext:2603.03251",
      "quote": "Speculative decoding focuses on reducing latency, and is generally ineffective for throughput-bound workloads",
      "claim": "The SSD authors identify throughput-bound workloads as a poor default fit for speculative decoding.",
      "relation": "challenges",
      "conditions": "Applies when added speculative and verification work meets an already compute-bound service.",
      "reported_result": "The excerpt gives this as an author-stated limitation; it also claims SSD can improve a latency-throughput frontier after accounting for extra hardware.",
      "transfer_inference": "The value of SSD on B200 depends on the actual latency, throughput, and hardware-cost objective.",
      "limitations": "The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash workload regime and SSD effect size are unknown."
    },
    {
      "source_id": "fulltext:2603.03251",
      "quote": "scaling the number of draft devices and thus the speculation cache",
      "claim": "The SSD authors identify additional draft devices and speculation-cache capacity as resources for further latency reduction.",
      "relation": "challenges",
      "conditions": "Scaling precomputed outcomes requires capacity for draft execution and cached speculations.",
      "reported_result": "The excerpt says returns eventually diminish; it gives no capacity or cost figure.",
      "transfer_inference": "A B200 evaluation must count draft compute, device capacity, and speculation-cache use against any saved latency.",
      "limitations": "Required device count, cache size, memory headroom, and cost for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash are unknown."
    },
    {
      "source_id": "github:vllm-project/vllm:36037",
      "quote": "If the actual verification result matches one of the predicted outcomes, the next speculation can be returned immediately",
      "claim": "A vLLM feature request describes the same conditional fast path and proposed overlap.",
      "relation": "context",
      "conditions": "The predicted outcomes must cover the actual verification result.",
      "reported_result": "The issue repeats paper-reported speedups; it supplies no vLLM measurement or implementation evidence.",
      "transfer_inference": "Outcome coverage is a key variable to measure for the target workload.",
      "limitations": "The supplied issue is closed with state reason “not_planned”; it does not show SSD support in vLLM."
    },
    {
      "source_id": "github:vllm-project/vllm:62541",
      "quote": "Full sweep run 38438383633 passed all 17 points and both evals",
      "claim": "A DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash B200 tuning PR reports validation of a specific FP4 MTP recipe.",
      "relation": "context",
      "conditions": "The PR concerns AgentX tuning settings for DEP2 and DEP4 concurrency points; it changes guide text only.",
      "reported_result": "The PR author reports 17 passing sweep points and two evals on the named vLLM nightly image.",
      "transfer_inference": "Those configured concurrency points could provide comparison workloads for an SSD experiment.",
      "limitations": "The PR is open and supplies no SSD result, measured draft/verify bubble, or SSD resource budget."
    },
    {
      "source_id": "github:vllm-project/vllm:62541",
      "quote": "32 GiB per DP rank, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.955`, `--max-num-seqs 48`",
      "claim": "The B200 guide PR describes host KV offload and a high GPU memory utilization setting for DEP2 c64/c128.",
      "relation": "challenges",
      "conditions": "These settings apply to the cited DEP2 host-KV configuration.",
      "reported_result": "The PR claims the recipe values were validated; it does not report free GPU memory.",
      "transfer_inference": "SSD speculation-cache and draft-state allocations need a capacity check alongside KV offload and graph capture.",
      "limitations": "Actual memory headroom and any SSD memory requirement are unknown."
    },
    {
      "source_id": "github:vllm-project/vllm:62073",
      "quote": "`max_num_seqs × (1 + num_speculative_tokens)` tokens per sequence-parallel rank",
      "claim": "An open MegaMoE PR describes a decode-workspace capacity that grows with speculative-token count.",
      "relation": "challenges",
      "conditions": "Its path uses FlashInfer nightly and applies when each DP rank's batch fits the decode-sized workspace.",
      "reported_result": "The PR reports a separate prefill-throughput comparison on 4×GB300; it says MegaMoE runtime paths still need CI or a nightly-FlashInfer machine.",
      "transfer_inference": "Increasing speculative work may raise per-rank workspace and warmup costs in a relevant MoE backend.",
      "limitations": "The throughput result is for Beam prefill, not DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash SSD on B200. Whether this backend and allocation apply to the target configuration is unknown."
    },
    {
      "source_id": "github:vllm-project/vllm:49620",
      "quote": "Preemption frees the request's KV state and resets its computed-token state, making that late output stale.",
      "claim": "An open vLLM fix identifies a correctness hazard when asynchronous speculative output arrives after preemption.",
      "relation": "challenges",
      "conditions": "A speculative frame is in flight when a request is preempted or its prefix cache is reset.",
      "reported_result": "The PR describes discarding stale output and accounting for a frame as `1 + num_scheduled_spec` placeholder tokens; its body lists a test plan, not a test result.",
      "transfer_inference": "An SSD integration must preserve request and KV-state identity across preemption, reject stale continuations, and account for all scheduled speculative placeholders.",
      "limitations": "The PR is open; correctness of this fix and its applicability to an SSD implementation are unverified in the supplied material."
    },
    {
      "source_id": "github:vllm-project/vllm:30980",
      "quote": "mean TPOT: 268.02 ms -> 260.72 = 2.7% speedup",
      "claim": "A different asynchronous vLLM change reported a modest TPOT improvement for DeepSeek-R1 with MTP and DP.",
      "relation": "context",
      "conditions": "The supplied benchmark used DP8, MTP with one speculative token, random prompts, and maximum request concurrency 2048.",
      "reported_result": "The PR reports mean TPOT falling 268.02→260.72 ms; its tables also show mean TTFT rising 20707.70→24249.12 ms.",
      "transfer_inference": "Asynchronous overlap can have different effects on latency metrics, so SSD should be evaluated at the intended concurrency and service objective.",
      "limitations": "This change overlaps DP coordination, not predicted-outcome speculation. Hardware is unknown; the PR is closed and unmerged. It does not measure a bottleneck on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash or B200."
    },
    {
      "source_id": "arxiv:2410.17375",
      "quote": "enables both models to perform predictions independently on separate devices",
      "claim": "The AMUSD abstract proposes continuous draft and verify work on separate devices and claims identical output quality.",
      "relation": "supports",
      "conditions": "Its asynchronous design uses separate devices.",
      "reported_result": "Abstract-level author claim: average 29% improvement over speculative decoding and up to 1.96× over autoregressive decoding.",
      "transfer_inference": "Separate-device execution is another plausible route to overlap, with an added device cost.",
      "limitations": "The abstract is not implementation or correctness evidence. Hardware, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash applicability, and B200 effect size are unknown."
    },
    {
      "source_id": "arxiv:2506.11309",
      "quote": "KV-cache inconsistencies, and communication overheads under small-batch tensor-parallelism",
      "claim": "The SwiftSpec abstract names state consistency and communication as obstacles to asynchronous speculative decoding.",
      "relation": "challenges",
      "conditions": "Its stated concern is low-latency, small-batch, tensor-parallel execution.",
      "reported_result": "The abstract claims a 1.75× average speedup across five model families and six datasets, and cites a Llama3-70B result on eight Hopper GPUs.",
      "transfer_inference": "A B200 design must check KV consistency and cross-device communication if it separates draft and verification.",
      "limitations": "Abstract claims are not implementation evidence. The cited model and Hopper setup differ from DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on B200."
    }
  ],
  "unanswered": [
    "Does the specified DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash B200 vLLM workload exhibit a measurable draft-after-verify stall, and how large is it?",
    "What are its verification-outcome distribution, usable precomputation hit rate, draft latency, and wasted speculation work?",
    "How much GPU memory, host memory, workspace, cache capacity, and additional device time would SSD require at the target concurrency points?",
    "What are SSD's measured TPOT, TTFT, throughput, and cost effects against the validated B200 MTP recipe?",
    "Which vLLM scheduler, KV-cache, preemption, graph-replay, and MoE paths would an SSD implementation use, and how would exact output correctness be verified?"
  ]
}
